page: Microsoft Azure E32pds_v7 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by 32 dedicated arm64 vCPUs combined with 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage provisions include an integrated 1890 GB local NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by compatibility with Azure Premium Storage for external disk volumes. The instance does not include graphical processing units or complimentary public IPv4 networking addresses.

The deployment of ARM64 architecture provides significant core density and qualitative operational cost efficiencies relative to traditional x86 hardware when servicing high-memory demands. By combining 256 GB of RAM with 1.89 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage, the machine delivers high localized I/O performance and extensive caching capacity directly on the host. An architectural tradeoff involves instruction-set compatibility, requiring application stacks and operating systems to natively support the ARM instruction set rather than x86 extensions.

This hardware balance makes the instance suited for memory-intensive and I/O-dependent enterprise deployments. Primary application profiles include large in-memory databases, distributed caching nodes, relational database management systems requiring rapid scratch space, data warehousing, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
